Unpacking the CT region of interest…
3D heart from the CT labels, with the virtual probe and beam (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom)
LV wallLV cavityRVLARAAortaPABeamScan edge, oesophagus
CT slice in the fan sector: what this probe position cuts

Probes and planes: each view plane is built from landmarks in the labels (valve centres where two labels touch, the LV apex and long axis). TTE probes sit where that plane meets the chest at the edge of the scan: the left sternal edge (parasternal), just beyond the apex (apical) and the lower front edge of the scan (subcostal); the suprasternal notch lies above the scan. TEE probes sit on the oesophagus centre line traced on this CT (mid-oesophageal) and under the inferior LV wall (transgastric). The venae cavae are not in the labels; their positions were read off the CT.

Fan sector: 90° wide, with a depth set for each view (11 to 17 cm); both can be changed. The image is the CT resliced along the beam plane. It is not an ultrasound simulation: there is no speckle, no shadow behind ribs or lung, and no loss of signal with depth. Dark blue marks where the beam is outside the CT scan.

Data: MM-WHS 2017 challenge (Zhuang et al.). The file contains a reduced copy of one CT scan, so it falls under the MM-WHS data access agreement: keep it for your own research and do not pass it on.
